episodes.170187: Several rounds of early evening thunderstorms on the 24th caused isolated pockets of tree damage across central Indiana with sub-severe hail also across Hendricks county.  By late into the evening, a series of storms moved across Knox county with areas of rainfall over 6 inches.  Significant flash flooding occurred across the county with a road washed out and water rescues conducted.
episodes.170238: A cold front and mid-level disturbance moved across a moderately unstable air mass during the late night hours of July 24th. Scattered showers and thunderstorms accompanied the cold front with a few isolated severe storms that produced damaging winds.
episodes.170240: A secondary cold front moved into a slightly unstable airmass across VT. A few thunderstorms developed along this front with one isolated thunderstorm that traveled along the international border with Canada. This storm intensified near Jay Peak and caused isolated wind damage near Lowell.
episodes.170260: An active moonsoon pattern continued across New Mexico on July 25, 2022, as a steady stream of moisture stayed in place over western and central New Mexico. Additionally, an easterly wave over northern Mexico that was trapped underneath the high pressure centered over the lower Mississippi Valley. An abundant amount of moisture in addition to this easterly wave resulted in robust thunderstorms across southern New Mexico that produced heavy rainfall. Socorro and Lincoln counties, including the McBride burn scar, were hit hardest with flash flooding.
episodes.170368: All of northern Ohio was located in the warm sector on the 23rd through most of the 24th. Simultaneously, a surface cold front drifted southeastward from the Upper Great Lakes and reached far-western Lake Erie, far-northwestern Ohio, and northeastern Indiana during the late evening of the 24th. This front finally swept southeastward through the rest of northern Ohio during the morning of the 25th. Multiple rounds of multicell thunderstorms occurred ahead of the cold front during the 23rd through wee hours of the 25th. Some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts as they encountered moderate MUCAPE and moderate to strong effective bulk shear and DCAPE, respectively.
episodes.170403: A cold front moved into the area, causing showers and thunderstorms. Some thunderstorms trained over the same area over southern Maryland, leading to instances of flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.170485: An upper-level trough moved into the Treasure State from the west. SPC placed several counties in a Marginal Risk for severe thunderstorms, including southern Judith Basin County, Meagher and Broadwater Counties, and northern Gallatin County with the remainder of the CWA under a general risk. Primary impact was heavy rain, but had possible lightning, small hail, and erratic winds associated with the storm.
episodes.170569: Widely scattered thunderstorms developed across northwestern Arkansas during the evening of the 24th. The strongest thunderstorm produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.170675: Afternoon and evening sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds over the coastal waters.
episodes.170678: A southeastward-moving cold front began crossing Lake Erie during the late evening of the 24th and neared the northeast Ohio and northwest Pennsylvania shore by the wee hours of the 25th. Multiple rounds of multicell thunderstorms impacted portions of the lakeshore in northern Ohio. Some of these storms produced gale-force peak wind gusts as they encountered moderate MUCAPE and moderate to strong effective bulk shear and DCAPE, respectively.
episodes.170679: Northwest Pennsylvania remained in the warm sector during the evening of the 24th through wee hours of the 25th as a cold front approached from the northwest. This front reached far-southern Lake Erie and northwestern Ohio by the wee hours of the 25th. Multiple rounds of multicell thunderstorms occurred ahead of the front. Some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts as they encountered moderate MUCAPE and moderate to strong effective bulk shear and DCAPE, respectively.
episodes.170695: Two rounds of convection impacted Pennsylvania on July 24, 2022. The first round of convection involved a cluster of storms that pushed across the northern mountains (along and north of I-80) during the afternoon hours, producing sporadic wind damage. The second round of convection was in the form of a line of thunderstorms just ahead of a cold front approaching northwestern Pennsylvania from the Great Lakes during the late evening of July 24 into the early morning hours of July 25. This second round of convection produced sporadic wind damage across northwestern Pennsylvania before weakening as it progressed southeastward overnight.
episodes.170780: An upper level ridge was over Southeast New Mexico. Low-level moisture was fairly high across the area. These conditions resulted in a thunderstorm that produced a severe wind gust in Eddy County.
episodes.170832: A weak cold front sparked scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms that resulted in several instances of damaging wind gusts. One storm in particular contained considerable hail and destructive winds just east of the City of Charlottesville.
episodes.170833: A weak cold front sparked scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms that resulted in several instances of damaging wind gusts. One storm in particular contained considerable hail and destructive winds just east of the City of Charlottesville.
episodes.170834: A weak cold front sparked scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms that resulted in several instances of damaging wind gusts. One storm in particular contained considerable hail and destructive winds just east of the City of Charlottesville.
episodes.170868: A weak cold front sparked scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms that resulted in many instances of gusty winds over area waterways.
episodes.171108: A line of thunderstorms moved across northern New Jersey and produced some isolated wind damage.
episodes.171109: An isolated thunderstorm produced some wind damage in Gloucester County.
episodes.171526: Monsoonal moisture streaming into the area, combined with slow moving thunderstorms, produced a narrow area of heavy rain from Black Hawk to Rapid Valley. Runoff from this rainfall caused minor street flooding on a few city streets in Rapid City, flooded open agricultural fields in Rapid Valley, and caused high flows and minor flooding along Rapid Creek.
episodes.171548: An isolated severe thunderstorm occurred across eastern Stillwater County and Southwest Yellowstone County during the early evening hours on the 24th. This thunderstorm produced large hail, very high wind gusts and torrential rain.
episodes.171824: Scattered thunderstorms developed along an outflow boundary near I-70 during the afternoon. As clusters of storms moved southeast during the evening, additional development behind the initial storms resulted in multiple rounds of thunderstorms over the same areas. More than 4 inches of rain fell in Lawrence County in six hours, producing isolated flash flooding. The storms also produced an isolated strong wind gust.
episodes.171908: An upper level ridge was centered over Arkansas. Although it was nearby, it wasn���t strong enough to provide enough subsidence to stop convective initiation. The morning KLIX upper air sounding showed a precipitable water over 2 inches. This time of year, unless the ridge is directly aloft, some storms will develop. That happened an one along a land-breeze boundary in Lake Pontchartrian produceda  waterspout. It remained offshore.
episodes.171945: During the late afternoon hours on July 24th, strong to severe thunderstorms developed across southeastern Illinois and southwestern Indiana ahead of a surface cold front located immediately to the northwest. Ahead of the cold front, temperatures across southwestern Indiana surged into the low-to-mid 90s during the afternoon on the 24th, with dewpoints residing in the mid-70s. This allowed for 3000-4000 J/kg of mixed-layer CAPE, leading to explosive convective development during the mid-to-late afternoon hours. By the time storms entered south central Indiana, decreased insolation reduced instability somewhat; however, storms were still strong enough to produce isolated wind damage across Dubois and Crawford County. As the cold front's forward progress had nearly stalled, the moist unstable air mass persisted over southern Indiana into the early overnight hours, leading to continued elevated convection which contributed to isolated flash flooding issues.
episodes.171954: A large area of rainfall slowly progressed east across East Central CO beginning in the late afternoon.  The first wave of rainfall included hail up to dime size that was reported north-northwest of Flagler.  Rain rates of over two inches per hour were reported near Flagler.  Total rainfall was up to four inches.  The prolonged torrential rainfall caused flooding in low lying areas over the west half of Kit Carson County, which lasted into the next day.  The rainfall was enough to fill the Flagler dam to capacity in one day. Meanwhile, as the event progressed a large area of rotation developed over Cheyenne County CO, moving northeast.  This allowed for an enhanced corridor of severe wind gusts to develop.  These winds uprooted a tree in Kit Carson, CO.  The strongest gust reported was 67 MPH near Firstview.
episodes.172083: A passing cold front combined with moderate shear and high instability resulted in multiple thunderstorms which produced several instances of wind damage across southwest Virginia.
episodes.172125: Severe thunderstorms developed within a hot and humid air mass across portions of eastern New York, especially for areas south of Interstate 90, during the afternoon and evening hours on July 24, 2022. Widespread wind damage occurred across these areas.||More than 20,000 customers lost power across Ulster and Dutchess counties including in Esopus, Rosendale, Kingston, Saugerties, Wawarsing, Hyde Park, Pleasant Valley and Poughkeepsie. Sporadic pockets of outages also occurred across the Capital Region and into portions of Rensselaer and Columbia counties.
episodes.172126: Severe thunderstorms developed within a hot and humid air mass across portions of western Massachusetts during the evening hours on July 24, 2022, producing sporadic wind damage.
episodes.172127: Severe thunderstorms developed within a hot and humid air mass across portions of northwestern Connecticut during the evening hours on July 24, 2022, producing sporadic wind damage.
episodes.172152: A few rounds of thunderstorms on July 24th and 25th preceded a cold frontal passage.  High levels of instability, ample shear, and pre-frontal disturbances provided thunderstorm clusters producing widespread damaging wind gusts.  Many instances of tree and power line damage were noted, along with isolated instances of structural damage.  One of those instances of structural damage, a tree falling on to two trailers in Venango County, unfortunately led to the death of a 28 year old woman.  Flash flooding of urbanized areas of Allegheny County also occurred.
episodes.172207: A weather system crossed Wyoming on July 24th, encouraging thunderstorm development. Severe thunderstorm winds occurred in multiple locations across northern and central Wyoming. At the Lander airport, a maximum wind gust of 74 mph was recorded. In Park County, wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph were reported. In Cody, 400 customers lost power when trees were downed by the wind and fell on power lines.
episodes.172294: Isolated thunderstorms once again occurred across the eastern plains. Damage was not widespread, though some significant damage did occur across the northwest portion of Prowers County.
episodes.172295: Thunderstorms occurred once again on this day, though coverage was lower. Large hail was observed, however, heavy rain with localized flooding were the main hazards.
episodes.172346: Several waves of convection moved through the region during the afternoon and first half of the ensuing night as a slow moving cold front approached from southern Ontario. The event was long lived due to high instability and strong shear. The first round of convection broke out along a lake breeze boundary that stretched from the Finger Lakes region back across the Southern Tier.  The next round of storms that developed after sunset produced wind damage and also very heavy rain. This was a rare event in that back to back severe thunderstorm watches were issued across the NWS Buffalo county warning area.
episodes.172347: Several waves of convection moved through the region during the afternoon and first half of the ensuing night as a slow moving cold front approached from southern Ontario. The event was long lived due to high instability and shear. The first round of convection broke out along a lake breeze boundary that stretched from the Finger Lakes region back across the Southern Tier.  The next round of storms that developed after sunset produced wind damage and also very heavy rain. This was a rare event in that back to back severe thunderstorm watches were issued across the NWS Buffalo county warning area.
episodes.172352: A shortwave and prefrontal trough resulted in a broken line of scattered severe thunderstorms which moved across central and eastern Virginia and into the Eastern Shore on July 25.
episodes.172353: A shortwave and prefrontal trough resulted in a broken line of scattered severe thunderstorms which moved across parts of Maryland on July 25.
episodes.172399: A surface lee trough over the Foothills of western North Carolina and the northwest Piedmont of central North Carolina led to the development of scattered afternoon and evening severe storms. Several of the storms produced wind damage and resultant downed trees and power lines. Storm activity waned by the late evening hours.
episodes.172447: An MCV situated in western Pima County on the morning of the 25th led to the development of showers/thunderstorms into Maricopa County. Deep monsoonal moisture, with PWATs in excess of 2 across south-central Arizona, allowed for showers/thunderstorms to be efficient rainfall producers leading to isolated flash flooding. A trained spotter near Arcacia Dr and 186th Dr reported 0.50 of rain in 20 minutes. To the south, flash flooding was reported in Waterman Wash, making roads impassable and leading to a water rescue. Additional heavy rainfall in the evening resulted in more isolated flash flooding. No injuries were reported.
episodes.172498: A combination of weak steering flow and tropical moisture resulted in slow moving thunderstorms with torrential downpours that produced flash flooding in Albany.  In addition, a few severe storms occurred with damaging winds.
episodes.172609: A passing cold front combined with high instability resulted in scattered thunderstorms across northwest North Carolina. One of these storms produced damaging winds in Surry County.
episodes.172613: A mid-level area of high shifted east and decreased in amplitude which opened the door for increased moisture, a classical medium to high end monsoonal pattern.
episodes.172632: Monsoonal moisture resulted in reports of flash flooding in portions of southern Utah.
episodes.172686: Scattered thunderstorms moved northwest across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. Storms produced heavy rain and flash flooding in Clifton, on the Tohono O'odham Nation and in western Pima County. Isolated flash flooding, wind damage and blowing dust occurred in other locations.
episodes.172761: Deep monsoon moisture remained across northern Arizona which allowed the formation of strong thunderstorms with heavy rain that produced flash flooding.
episodes.172796: Summer diurnal thunderstorms moved slowly and produced localized heavy rainfall amounts.
episodes.172800: Thunderstorms moving offshore brought gusty winds to the waters east of Portsmouth.
episodes.172801: A cold front moved eastward from the Great Lakes states and into New England on the 25th. The front was preceded by plenty of heat and instability to foster a few strong to severe thunderstorms.
episodes.172803: A cold front moved eastward from the Great Lakes states and into New England on the 25th. The front was preceded by plenty of heat and instability to foster a few strong to severe thunderstorms.
episodes.172892: Low pressure over eastern Canada dragged a cold front through southeastern NY. A pre-frontal trough ahead of the cold front was able to spark severe thunderstorms that produced large hail. More severe thunderstorms developed along the cold front and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.172910: A big push of monsoon moisture immediately followed the excessive heat event, and stormy conditions persisted into August. Many storms produced flash flooding, and some produced severe weather.
episodes.172912: A big push of monsoon moisture immediately followed the excessive heat event, and stormy conditions persisted into August. Several storms produced severe weather and flash flooding.
episodes.172955: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed over western North Carolina during the afternoon and evening. Several of the storms produced strong-to-damaging wind gusts.

Forest thinning in the Magdalena Mountains resulted in a flash flooding event that made it easier for water to rush down an unnamed canyon. Floodwaters left behind a pile of debris 6 feet high and 20 feet wide that included steel fence posts and barbed wire, damaged trailed, and boulders that were 200 to 300 pounds. Damages are estimated.

A thunderstorm produced heavy rainfall in the high terrain around the town of Hildale, as well as within the town itself. Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor (MRMS) 1-hour estimates showed around 1 to 2 inches of rainfall with this storm. Light to moderate rain continued for a while thereafter, with 3-hour MRMS estimates exceeding 2 inches of rainfall in spots. This rainfall ran into Short Creek, and resulted in a flow through the town of Hildale, though the flow was not significant enough to overtop any road crossings within town.
